# odyssey-081 (16.393–481) — review

Reviewer: adversarial, two passes. `t` untouched (checked: every unit's `t` identical to the draft, and the `t` of all 58 units joins to the 89 packet lines). `l` keeps the line division of `t` in every unit; no `\n` in any `i`. `gloss.json` does not exist yet, so there was nothing to check; the second pass could not read it. Scansion: the packet flags no lines, so no hand scan was required and no note was added.

Unit references are by first line (`ln`) and, where two units share a line, by order (461a = "ἦλθες, δῖ’ Εὔμαιε.", 461b = "τί δὴ κλέος …;"; 470a, 470b likewise).

Counts. Pass 1: high 2, medium 10, low 12, nit 5 (29 changes). Pass 2: high 0, medium 0, low 1, nit 0 (1 change; 1 nit refused). Totals: high 2, medium 10, low 13, nit 5.

## Checks that passed (no change)

- Quotation marks: five speeches, each “ on its first unit and ” on its last, in both `l` and `i` (5 and 5 in each layer): 400–405, 418–433, 435–447, 461–463 (461a … 462), 465–475. `mark` on the first unit of each: "Amphinomus speaks", "Penelope speaks", "Eurymachus answers", "Telemachus speaks", "Eumaeus answers". The last unit of odyssey-080 (16.389–391) closes its speech with ”, so the opening unit 393 ("ὣς ἔφαθ’ …") is narration and no run-on speech enters this part; no speech runs into 16.482.
- `p: true` on 393, 400, 406, 409, 418, 434, 448, 452, 464, 476, 478: exactly Murray's ¶ lines.
- Whole-unit repeats match the published `l`/`i` exactly: 393, 464. Line-level repeats reuse the published wording: 407, 415–416, 436, 450–451, 480.
- Shipped house renderings followed: ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπε, δῖα γυναικῶν, ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζεν, τὴν δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύμαχος … ἀντίον ηὔδα (existing row, masculine → feminine), περίφρων / ἐχέφρων kept apart, δῖος ὑφορβός, μνηστῆρες ἀγήνορες, ἱερὴ ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο (l "force", i "the strong, sacred figure"), θάνατόν τε μόρον τε "death and doom", κούρη Ἰκαρίοιο "daughter" (noun-phrase, not the vocative κούρη "maiden"), θέμιστες "rules of right", πολύπυρος "rich in wheat", φαίδιμος "glorious", σιγαλόεις "glossy", ἐσάντα "face to face", οἶνος ἐρυθρός "red wine", αἷμα κελαινόν "dark blood", ὠκύς "swift", νηῦς θοή "swift ship", ὑπέρβιον "exceeding".

## Findings considered and refused

- ἔσχεθεν "restrained" (the drafter's uncertain item). The draft's l "restrained" is the same as shipped odyssey-016 l; only i differed and was fixed (see change, 430). The glossary already has ἔσχεθεν as "restrained, checked". No other published part contains ἔσχεθ-.
- 394 i "who came from Dulichium": "came" is not in the Greek (ἐκ Δουλιχίου goes with ἡγεῖτο, "led from D."). Kept: it is the shortest English for "leader from D." and the note says the verb is ἡγεῖτο. Not a force change.
- 398 κέχρητ’ perfect rendered "had" in i vs "makes use of" in l. Kept: perfect of χράομαι with present sense, and the clause gives the reason; l and i agree in sense.
- 409 i and 462 i omit αὖτ’ ("in turn") that l keeps: i may drop a weak particle; kept.
- 411 i "had learned" against l "was learning" (πεύθετο imperfect); 412 the same. Kept: narrative past, and 412's ἐπεύθετο gets the same pair, so the two are consistent.
- 428 i "tear the life from him" for ἀπορραῖσαι φίλον ἦτορ (l "tear away his dear heart"). Considered changing to "heart"; refused: the note names the metonymy, the table already allows φίλον ἦτορ to be dropped from `i` ("dear heart" in `l`, dropped in `i`), and "tear the heart from him" is not an English idiom for killing.
- 428 πολλήν as "abundant": follows the new-renderings row; the shipped ζωή "livelihood" (066) and "estate" (068) are different contexts and the row's "living" is explained.
- 445 "That is why" for τῷ and 447 "what comes from the gods" for θεόθεν: idiomatic renderings of a pronoun-adverb and a -θεν adverb; l keeps the literal, the sense agrees.
- 448 i "though he himself was preparing destruction for him": "him" twice could confuse; refused, because the Greek τῷ … αὐτός has the same shape and the note names both.
- 452 ἑσπέριος "adjective used as an adverb" (it agrees with ὑφορβός and so is predicative "in the evening"); the old and the new label amount to the same English, and the table's rendering is "at evening"/"in the evening". Kept.
- 453 ἐπισταδόν "standing by": the sense is uncertain in the lexica; the table already has ἐπισταδόν (12.392) "standing by", so the draft's new row follows it and no flag is needed.
- 456 note "ποίησε having dropped its augment" and 464 etc.: correct (ἐποίησε); kept.
- 462 ἦ ῥ’ taken as a question particle, not the speech-closing ἦ ῥα: correct, kept.
- 472–474 ἀμφίγυοισι "meaning not known" with "double-pointed": said to be unknown, rendered with the usual guess, and the new-renderings row says so; matches the rule on unknown words.
- 427 and 432 ἀκαχίζω "grieved"/"cause great grief": follows the new-renderings row; the table has no conflicting row.
- 425 δῆμον "people": the table fixes δῆμος "land" for δήμῳ ἐν …, but "having feared the land" is not sense. The note says "the people of the land, not the land itself". A new-renderings row was added so the exception is on record (see below).
- Capital after an ano teleia at unit starts 428, 433, 441  ("They wished …" after a unit ending in ";"): each unit is a sense-unit that starts a sentence-like block after Murray's ·; the draft capitalises these consistently. Nit, refused.
- 478 θυμός "heart" in l (singular) against i "hearts": the new-renderings row records both; each is plain English for the distributive plural.
- 404 κτενέω … "kill him": "him" is supplied in i with the note saying the object is unspoken; correct.

## Pass 2 (gloss parses)

Scope: all 89 novel entries and the 12 `__broaden__` entries in `gloss.json`, each checked against every occurrence in `units.json` (case, number, tense, mood, voice, lemma, Attic equivalent, possessive ὅς against relative, article-forms as pronouns). Modern translations not opened. After the edits: valid UTF-8 JSON, every novel entry under 230 characters (longest 157), only typographic ’, no line numbers, no "here".

Counts. Entries checked 101 (89 novel, 12 broadened). Changed 14 (13 novel, 1 broadened). Refused 4 (μάρτυρος, εἰρώμεθα, ἔλθοι, κεν; the other bullets under Refused record checks that found nothing to change). Unchanged: 87, of which 4 are the refusals.

### Changes made

- ἄτιμον: gloss said "without redress … ’unavenged’", against the unit's "dishonoured" (l, i, note: ἄτιμος "without honour") and the new-renderings row that refuses "unrequited". Now "without honour, dishonoured … ’dishonoured’".
- ἀποκτείνεις: gloss gave ’you kill’; the unit renders "seek to kill" and the note says it is conative. Now "pres. 2 sg., conative … ’you seek to kill’".
- ἀρητιάδαο: gloss said "son of Aretus", the unit (l, note) has "Aretes’ son". Now "son of Aretes", and the gloss says it agrees with Νίσου.
- ἀμφιγύοισι: gloss offered "’strong’ or ’two-pointed’"; the unit says the meaning is not known with "pointed at both ends" as the usual guess, and the new-renderings row refuses "strong-limbed". Now "meaning not known (the usual guess is ’pointed at both ends’)"; Attic -οις added; agreement with ἔγχεσιν (neut. dat. pl.) stated.
- ἀνώξω: quote ’I will bid’ replaced by ’I will urge on’ (the unit's l and i).
- ἐρωήσει: "rush, gush, spurt … ’will spurt’" made "rush, gush … ’will gush’", as in l and the note. Parse (future of ἐρωέω, 3 sg.) confirmed.
- ἐπέσχε: quote ’held to’ replaced by ’held out’ (l, i, note). Parse (aor. 3 sg. of ἐπέχω) confirmed.
- ἤκαχε: quote ’vexed’ replaced by ’grieved’ (l, note, and the new-renderings row).
- ἐϋφρονέων: gloss said "kindly-minded, mean well … ’with good will’"; the unit's l is "well-disposed in mind" and the new-renderings row refuses the first-draft "good intent". Now "well-minded, well-disposed … ’well-disposed’", with Attic εὐφρονῶν named.
- ὁσίη: gloss gave ’it is lawful’, which new-renderings refuses; l "holy", i "right". Now ’it is holy, it is right’.
- τρομέεσθαι: parsed "pres. inf." under the active τρομέω; -εσθαι is the middle infinitive. Now "τρομέω (mid. τρομέομαι) … pres. inf. mid., epic uncontracted -έεσθαι (= Attic -εῖσθαι)".
- ἐπισταδὸν: the shipped glossary has ἐπισταδόν as "one after another, standing close by"; the novel entry (grave-accent form) gave only "standing by, standing about". Now "standing by, standing close … also read ’one after another’", with the derivation. l/i "standing by" unchanged.
- εἰρύσσαιτο: lemma, voice, tense and mood kept (aor. opt. 3 sg. mid., as the unit's note). Added the Attic equivalent (= ἐρύσαιτο) and that the optative continues the μή clause, so the form is anchored to the line.
- εἰρύαται (broadened): the added half said "perf. mid. 3 pl." while the unit's note calls it a present; now "perf. mid. 3 pl. with pres. sense, epic -αται (for -νται)", which agrees with both the old half and the note.

### Refused

- μάρτυρος: kept as "o-stem by-form of Attic μάρτυς; masc. nom. sg., predicative". It agrees with the note (μάρτυρος stands where μάρτυς is usual; Ζεὺς … ἐστί understood). The form is rare and the lexicon treatment is not checked here, so no claim beyond the note was added.
- εἰρώμεθα: gloss names Attic ἐρώμεθα and says present subjunctive of ἔρομαι (ἐρέομαι); the note names Attic ἐρέσθαι. Both are in use for the same Homeric form (present subjunctive of εἴρομαι, or aorist subjunctive of the same root). Mood, person, voice and meaning agree with the unit; kept.
- ἐπισταδὸν sense: whether it means "standing by" or "one after another" is not settled; both are now in the entry, and neither is asserted as the only one.
- ἔλθοι (broadened): added clause says ’lest he go’ for μή … ἔλθοι ἀπαγγέλλων, while l has "come reporting". The note and i say "go", the entry is a gloss of the lemma ἔρχομαι "go, come", and the optative after μή is correctly named; kept.
- κεν (broadened): the added clause ("fut. indic. in a relative clause … ὅς κεν … ἐποίσει") matches the note, which calls ἐποίσει a future. ἐποίσει could also be read as a short-vowel subjunctive; the note decides, and the entry's older clause already allows "fut. indic. or short-vowel subj." in an apodosis. Kept; the older "ἤ κεν … κτεῖνεν" clause ("future event pictured as already accomplished" with a past-tense gloss) is not from this part and was left alone.
- κ, θ, μεθ, μετὰ, πόνου, σφέας, τούς, ἐΐσης, δαιτὸς (broadened): each new clause checked against its occurrence (403 and 405 εἰ … κ’ + aor. subj.; ὅθι θ’; μεθ’ ὁμήλικας + acc. "among"; μετὰ φρεσὶ σῇσι + dat. "in"; παύσαντο πόνου + gen.; σφέας … ἔμμεναι acc. subject of an infinitive; τούς τ’ ἄλλους "the others"; δαιτὸς ἐΐσης after ἐδεύετο). All correct, no change.
- Pronoun and possessive checks: οἷσιν (possessive ὅς, "his own"), τοῦ ("his", demonstrative, not possessive ὅς) and οὗ are not gloss keys and need no entry; the keys τούς, σφέας, ὅ-forms are glossed as pronouns. Nothing to change.
